values.goal: Distinguish logical coordinates from pixels and build a time-based Canvas editor yourself.
values.capstone: A canvas lab with shape editing, undo, particle previews, PNG/JSON saving, and a comparison report

values.title: Coordinates and Pixels
values.prerequisites: You should be able to work with JavaScript functions and arrays, DOM events, and coordinates.
values.environment: The existing built-in example provides only a starting point. It does not implement all extended requirements. Implement this yourself in an HTML and ES module project on a separate local HTTP development server. Record the browser version, viewport, and DPR.
values.concepts.0.title: CSS and the Buffer
values.concepts.0.explanation: CSS dimensions control layout, while width and height specify the pixel buffer dimensions. Increase the buffer by DPR and transform logical coordinates to draw at the same size with greater sharpness.
values.concepts.1.title: Resetting State
values.concepts.1.explanation: Assigning canvas.width resets the image and drawing state. Setting the scale again with setTransform on resize avoids repeated scaling.
values.outcomes.0: Output the CSS dimensions and buffer dimensions separately.
values.outcomes.1: The circle's center and radius remain unchanged after resizing.
values.steps.0: Prepare day-01.js and index.html in the external practice project. Set the canvas CSS size to 400×240 and draw a grid and circle with getContext('2d').
values.steps.1: Set the buffer to CSS size×DPR, apply setTransform(DPR,0,0,DPR,0,0), and show the actual buffer dimensions in output.
values.steps.2: Save the output with the input condition 1, then run again with 2. Expected: Logical shape sizes stay the same, and the number of buffer pixels becomes four times larger. Compare this with the actual screen and logs, and record the actual results and reasons for differences in day-01-notes.md.
values.variables.0.name: DPR
values.variables.0.expected: Logical shape sizes stay the same, and the number of buffer pixels becomes four times larger
values.criteria.0: Output the CSS dimensions and buffer dimensions separately.
values.criteria.1: The circle's center and radius remain unchanged after resizing.
values.questions.0: Why do shapes become smaller if you only double the buffer dimensions?
values.questions.1: What goes wrong if scale accumulates on every resize?
